sentences: `uint mask; entries[mask+1] of 10 uints: key[0..7], index, pad`.
The key is a T# or a padded S#.
FNV-1a over the eight key words selects the first slot.
The shared SPIR-V lookup probes up to eight slots and returns index 0 on a miss.
The runtime supplies a fallback at index 0 and maps live descriptor keys to bindless indices.
Outside the wave64 emulation, the lookup's result goes through `OpGroupNonUniformBroadcastFirst` before it indexes the image or sampler array.
The lookup key words come from SGPRs, so every invocation in a subgroup has the same index; the broadcast is an identity on all drivers and marks the value uniform for the compiler.
It declares `GroupNonUniform` and `GroupNonUniformBallot`, without a shuffle capability or subgroup-lane input.
The shader index records the capabilities; its `features` field lists optional Vulkan device features.

Mesa ANV 26.2.7 on an Intel Alder Lake-S UHD (Xe-LP, Linux) segfaults in `vkCreate*Pipelines` on a sampler index taken straight from the probe loop when that sampler serves both a float and an integer image (`cs_sample_lz_int_d16`, `ps_ssharp`); with the broadcast both pass.
